skill.name: rn-state-flows
skill.description: Guides React Native teams through complex multi-step async flows using explicit states, transitions, validation, error handling, and integration tests.
skill.summary: Design, implement, debug, and test React Native state flows with explicit transition patterns.
skill.author: CJHarmath

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives after reviewing SKILL.md. The skill is documentation for React Native async flow design and includes TypeScript examples, Markdown fences, logging templates, and tests; no command execution, secret handling, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: No security fix is required. Authors can reduce scanner noise by keeping examples clearly labeled as TypeScript or Markdown documentation.

content.value_statement: Complex React Native flows can fail when async steps, state updates, and UI feedback are not modeled clearly. This skill gives structured patterns for explicit flow states, validations, logging, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to model multi-step React Native operations as explicit states and transitions.
Provides TypeScript examples for ordered async flow execution with validation after each step.
Shows how to track flow state in a store for loading, ready, complete, and error UI states.
Includes integration test patterns for happy paths and failures at individual flow steps.
Offers a checklist for designing, implementing, testing, and documenting complex flows.
Gives criteria for deciding when to use XState instead of simpler explicit flow code.
limitations: It is guidance-only and does not include executable package code or automation scripts.
Examples are centered on React Native assessment retake flows and may need adaptation.
It does not implement a complete XState machine or install any state management library.
It does not replace project-specific testing for real APIs, storage, and navigation behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan an Async Feature Flow
use_cases.description: Map each step, precondition, postcondition, and error transition before coding a React Native feature.

use_cases.title: Debug Flow Ordering Bugs
use_cases.description: Inspect missing awaits, invalid transitions, and weak postcondition checks in a multi-step flow.

use_cases.title: Review Flow Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Create integration tests that verify happy paths, persisted state, and failures at each async step.

prompt_templates.title: Sketch a Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new feature flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rn-state-flows skill to outline states, transitions, preconditions, postconditions, and error states for this React Native flow: [describe feature].

prompt_templates.title: Convert Code to Explicit Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor of an existing async function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply rn-state-flows patterns to refactor this React Native async function into explicit ordered steps with validation and error handling: [paste code].

prompt_templates.title: Add UI Flow State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use rn-state-flows to design store state and component rendering for loading, ready, submitting, complete, and error states in this screen: [describe screen].

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Test a Complex Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a React Native reviewer using rn-state-flows. Find ordering risks, missing postconditions, weak error transitions, and integration test gaps in this flow: [paste flow and tests].

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to implement a five-step retake flow with answer loading, retake enablement, answer clearing, user input, and submit.
output_examples.output: The response identifies each flow state, lists required preconditions and postconditions, recommends ordered async execution, and defines error states for retry or exit.

output_examples.input: A team reports that answers disappear after a user restarts a React Native assessment flow.
output_examples.output: The response traces likely ordering failures, suggests validation after loading and clearing steps, and proposes an integration test that verifies answer persistence.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a project should use XState for a branching mobile flow.
output_examples.output: The response compares state count, branching complexity, visualization needs, and team sharing requirements before recommending either explicit steps or XState.

best_practices: Document every flow state with its preconditions, action, postconditions, and error handling.
Validate state after each async step and log transitions with a flow identifier.
Write integration tests for the happy path and for failures at each important step.
anti_patterns: Starting dependent async steps without awaiting the previous required state update.
Keeping flow state implicit across scattered functions with no transition model.
Testing only isolated functions while ignoring full user journeys and failure paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design and debug complex React Native flows with ordered async steps, explicit states, validation, and tests.

faq.question: Does it require XState?
faq.answer: No. It explains when simple explicit flow code is enough and when XState may be worth using.

faq.question: Can I use it with Zustand?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show store-based flow state that fits Zustand-style React Native state management.

faq.question: Does it run code or modify my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with examples and checklists. Any code changes must be made by your agent or developer.

faq.question: What tests does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends integration tests for the complete happy path and targeted tests for errors at each flow step.

faq.question: Is it only for assessment retake flows?
faq.answer: No. The examples use retake flows, but the patterns apply to checkout, onboarding, sync, upload, and other multi-step flows.
